answer.answer: The completed import is reconciled and checkpointed without creating a second canonical game-data snapshot. Durable checkpoint: checkpoint:efa4d9fd-6a5b-1fb9-3b3c-b9b82fa662b7.

claims.value: The original `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` (21,674,717 bytes; SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3`) and a verified extracted tree are retained unchanged under ignored `raw/`. The ZIP has 123 entries including directories; all 115 manifested files passed the package checksum ledger, and `unzip -t` passed. `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` remain tracked for auditability. The ignored raw material includes the duplicate third-party corpus, personalized save context, generated binaries, legacy SQLite database, source snapshot JSON, core delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh script, and query script. Key retained hashes include legacy SQLite `d9ffbae20414d9e05a5dc02a664c904bc2bf0b8d74c8ae427ee9e8dccf6669fc`, snapshot JSON `373e0f0dc556ce9cc03120321356bf7ce85fc012ffd7b49ce1aac3e89e6abf59`, and workbook `2cb9f89360b9a721b2f41771ac77643a0438cb27e96b4f84a161ba93e7e04263`.

The archive’s repeated association of its numeric data with Steam build `23761620` is corrected: that identifier denotes only the latest public executable observed—Update 1 Hotfix `0.2.8`—and is not proven provenance for every archived value. The authoritative two-axis boundary is (1) game data: Update 1 internal version `35118973`, dated 2026-04-09 and contextually mapped to Steam build `22674441` / inferred `0.2.0`; and (2) source capture: SRDB `2.3.4`, retrieved 2026-07-11 05:02:30 UTC. The sole current immutable snapshot is `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`. Archive retrieval was `2026-07-08T19:01:37Z`; its source-site version and reliable numeric-data build identity were not recorded. Its legacy calculations must retain that boundary until actually ported and rerun against the canonical snapshot.

The archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset were semantic duplicates of the richer RuptureOps corpus and were not installed as a competing snapshot. Selective promotion was limited to the player save baseline `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json`; six medium-confidence Ore Excavator v2 impure/pure recipe-producer associations; medium-confidence consumable-effect assumptions kept separate from raw item records with explicit provenance warnings; nine player-specific site/geography assets; and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. Reconciliation also corrected two normalization defects: `airlock` had been overwritten by a building-shaped detail response, and Training Corporation contained a literal `$undefined` index. The active corpus still reports 48 raw recipes without producer associations; the six promoted overrides leave 42 unresolved, which remain `incomplete` production with named recipe IDs rather than being treated as raw inputs.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family is preserved only as superseded audit history; it over-rotated toward buffers and must not become current guidance. The active authority is the RuptureOps pipeline/database and the July 11 staged Flowworks note. That plan is proposed construction, not confirmed installed state: the starter has one each of Titanium Excavator, Wolfram Excavator, Titanium Smelter, Wolfram Smelter, Titanium Rod v2, Wolfram Powder v2, Wolfram Plate v2, Stabilizer, Impeller, and Turbine; the Valve expansion adds one Titanium Smelter, Sheet v2, Beam, Housing, Nozzle, and two Valves, with a second v1 Titanium Excavator only for an Impure selected node; the Pressure Tank stage adds two Pumps; the second Stabilizer waits until before Scanner/levels 11–12; and one HRS v2 pad is reserved but built only if imported-HRS recovery fails in practice. Rejected defaults that remain inactive without new evidence include the five-output-depot bank, a second permanent HRS export depot, a prebuilt separate Helium rail, campaign-scale Acid as a universal trunk, a third Faraday Supermagnet Furnace, and the assumption that Grand Basin’s five families require exactly five Cores.

answer.answer: Landmark-grounded geography checkpoint completed and persisted. Grand Basin is corrected to the basin beside Mythic Cry; relational pins remain relational; screenshot and SRDB coordinate frames remain separate.

claims.value: Grand Basin Reserve is the broad basin immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry” and north of the active production corridor. This supersedes the incorrect provisional Red Lake/Redleaf match. The marker denotes the basin region, not a future Core; its first campus should remain east of the mountain/POI boundary, with a combat exclusion strip preserved beside Mythic Cry.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Flowworks is a selected but unbuilt site between Landerworks and Faraday: east/northeast of Landerworks and west/northwest of Faraday. It lies on the active Landerworks–Faraday relationship axis, but no Core, production placement, or surveyed connecting track is confirmed.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: The overview’s site pins were registered visually against screenshot terrain, whereas planning-note coordinates identify SRDB markers; no verified transform connects those frames, so they must not be combined. The dashed Landerworks–Flowworks–Faraday axis expresses relative placement rather than surveyed rail geometry. Sunstone Station and Brimstone Utility likewise have known parent-site relationships but no registered exact pins. GRO “Mythic Cry” at approximately `2518.767,3099.107` and the Geo Scanner near `3059,2618` are SRDB-marker references, not transformed screenshot-pin coordinates.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: The first Goethite satellite should use the safer triple northwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin; the first Oil satellite should use the preferred site west/southwest of Grand Basin. These remain landmark-relative directions because no verified coordinate-frame transform exists. The satellite requirement is substantive: neither Goethite nor Oil is onsite at Grand Basin. The retrieved evidence labels these choices “safer” and “preferred,” but does not establish a fuller comparative hazard or logistics rationale.

answer.answer: Resume the July 11 canonical staged Flowworks build. Its modeled post-second-Stabilizer import peak is 252/min, so one 480/min Rail v3 trunk fits with 228/min nameplate headroom. Use buffers for burst smoothing and recovery, not as substitutes for capacity; reserve HRS v2 and install it only after measured imported-HRS recovery failure.

claims.value: The canonical starter is a planned 10-machine build, including extractors: 1 Titanium Excavator, 1 Wolfram Excavator, 1 Titanium Smelter, 1 Wolfram Smelter, 1 Titanium Rod v2, 1 Wolfram Powder v2, 1 Wolfram Plate v2, 1 Stabilizer, 1 Impeller, and 1 Turbine. It is the adopted plan, not confirmed construction.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - progression and next builds.md

claims.value: After adding the second Stabilizer, peak imported refill demand is HRS 54/min + Helium-3 72/min + Sulphuric Acid 56/min + Rotor 60/min + Stator 10/min = 252/min.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - progression and next builds.md

claims.value: Yes—one Rail v3 trunk fits: 252/min peak refill demand is below its 480/min capacity, leaving 228/min of nameplate headroom before buffer smoothing. Flowworks makes Titanium Rod and Wolfram Plate locally; world freight terminates at one storage-yard spur rather than traversing the machine network. Reserve a second right-of-way, but split only if stocked sources coexist with slow destination recovery.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - progression and next builds.md

answer.answer: The duplicate archive-import lanes are coordinated around the existing canonical reconciliation. No repository changes or additional promotions were made, and one continuation checkpoint was committed.

claims.value: Seven related sessions are recorded: 019f4f6d-169c-70e2-8de4-81722b41eee9 (initial Update 1 research/bootstrap), 019f5263-8bae-7d10-b944-0fd4a543afb9 (clean bootstrap and ownership split), 019f52a5-72aa-7c11-853c-5de258361b42 (general import/reconciliation), 019f52fa-6195-7701-96a2-da6ec7ef7a08 (live exploration continuation), 019f52fa-6917-78a3-b1e5-7e631263b4a5 (logistics fork), 019f52fa-7180-7552-a3b1-09be4c3ee493 (exploration fork carrying the same inherited import request), and 019f531d-ba10-7d50-958e-4cffc089c334 (timer research/build). The logistics and exploration forks inherited the same Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip request and therefore represent duplicate execution lanes, not independent imports or corroboration.

Idempotent identity is the verified source archive SHA-256 1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3 together with import_id star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z. The receipt records imported_at 2026-07-11T19:54:52Z, byte_size 21674717, 115 manifested files, CHECKSUMS.sha256, and integrity_status verified. A matching request is a replay: use the immutable manifest/checksums and existing reconciliation receipt instead of importing or promoting again.

The one successful reconciliation is canonical. The archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset were semantically duplicated by the richer corpus and were not installed as a competing snapshot. Only the player-save baseline, six Ore Excavator v2 associations, consumable-effect assumptions, nine player geography assets, consolidated vault notes, and two normalization corrections were promoted. Separately, historical evidence says the iOS timer began on dirty main with new work under ios/ and had not passed its simulator/install-ready gate. Preserve that work in place: do not branch, stash, reset, overwrite, or mix another archive promotion into it. Because access was restricted to ./memory, dirty main is historical evidence rather than freshly verified Git status.

Exactly one continuation checkpoint was committed: checkpoint:b738a186-e311-bc69-7f98-af86666b6618 at .straylight/checkpoints/b738a186-e311-bc69-7f98-af86666b6618.md. Every duplicate fork should reopen it, designate one coordinator, verify live Git status read-only when repository access is authorized, and return the existing receipt whenever the import ID and archive hash match. No additional import, promotion, repository edit, or promotion checkpoint was created in this run.
